The first Markdown line must be '# ' followed by the actual paper title, not the literal placeholder 'Title'. Plans, previous_work and review feedback cannot override this publication contract.

raw_content:
The task: plan a short literature review on cost models. Language: Chinese by default. Return exactly one JSON object, no code fences.

Need to produce: round, questions, queries (crossref/arxiv), inclusion_criteria, exclusion_criteria, revision_tasks, previous_work (null since empty snapshot).

"cost models" is ambiguous — could be cost models in software engineering (COCOMO), cloud computing cost models, cost models in electricity/power systems, healthcare cost models, machine learning cost models. Scope is short literature review. I should keep scope answerable, distinguish requested scope from accessible. I should perhaps note ambiguity in revision_tasks — but planning should define a scope. Let me pick a defensible scope: 成本模型 (cost models) with focus on 软件/云计算/系统资源成本建模? Given ambiguity, I should state a primary interpretation and note alternatives in revision_tasks. Perhaps better: define scope broadly but with sub-questions, and queries covering several domains so the writer can narrow.

Hmm, but a short review needs focus. I'll define the core scope as "成本模型的构建与估计方法" spanning 软件工程成本估算 (COCOMO 等算法成本模型)、云/分布式系统资源成本模型、以及数据驱动的成本预测模型, with inclusion criteria requiring explicit cost model formulation. Actually that could be too broad. Let me instead frame questions around: (1) 成本模型的主要类型与建模范式, (2) 参数化/算法模型 (COCOMO, 功能点) 的构成与校准, (3) 数据驱动/机器学习成本预测, (4) 云与服务计算中的成本模型 (TCO, 定价/资源分配), (5) 验证与评估指标 (MMRE, PRED(25)) 及局限。

I should keep queries reasonable: a few per source. Crossref doesn't index arXiv well; arXiv covers CS. For cost models in software engineering, Crossref good. Let's produce ~8-10 queries.

Note: Crossref queries as plain search strings. arXiv query syntax can be plain text with field prefixes; I'll write arXiv-style queries like `all:"cost model" AND all:"software cost estimation"`.

Include previous_work: null.

revision_tasks: instructions for the writer — e.g., 标题、摘要、结构、引用规范、不写 References、注意区分成本模型类型、避免交叉领域混淆、标注不确定范围等.

Let me write JSON with Chinese prose.

round: 1.

questions: array of objects? Spec says questions: [...] — ambiguous. Could be list of strings or objects with id/question. I'll use objects with id and question — hmm, safer to use objects with "id" and "question"? The spec just says questions: [...]. Many implementations use strings. I'll use objects {id, question} for clarity... Risk: schema validation expecting strings. Hmm. The description says "Define research questions" — I'll use objects with id and question, that's more informative and commonly tolerated. Actually to reduce risk, maybe use strings with prefix "RQ1: ...". I'll go with objects {id, question} — I think it's fine. Hmm, let me choose strings prefixed "RQ1：" to be safest? Objects give structure. I'll go with objects; they're self-describing.

Actually, thinking about downstream writers: questions as objects with id/question is quite standard in these multi-agent review systems. I'll do that.

inclusion_criteria / exclusion_criteria: arrays of strings in Chinese.

revision_tasks: array of strings (tasks for the writing node).

Also maybe include a "scope_notes" — not in schema, avoid. Keep only specified keys: round, questions, queries, inclusion_criteria, exclusion_criteria, revision_tasks, previous_work. Adding extra keys could violate "exactly one JSON object" — extra keys probably fine but better keep to spec. I'll fold scope caveats into revision_tasks and questions.

Write it.
